developments.title: GLM 5.3 Flash Support Integrated into DwarfStar Main Branch
detail: GLM 5.3 Flash support has been merged into the DwarfStar main branch, bringing vision capabilities to the model. The update also includes SSD streaming improvements and prepares DS4 Flash vision support and new checkpoints for upcoming releases.
developments.why_it_matters: The integration lets DwarfStar users run vision‑enabled GLM 5.3 models with Flash acceleration, delivering faster inference for AI workloads on supported hardware.

developments.title: pi-mcp-adapter Added to Official Notion MCP Documentation
detail: The pi-mcp-adapter repository, which provides a token‑efficient MCP adapter for the Pi coding agent, is now listed in Notion’s official MCP documentation.
The Notion developers page on connecting an MCP client now references the adapter, giving users a clear, supported path to integrate the tool with their Notion workspace.
developments.why_it_matters: Having the adapter documented by Notion gives developers immediate, authoritative guidance for using pi-mcp-adapter, reducing integration friction and promoting wider adoption of the Pi coding agent.

developments.title: Pinggy publishes comprehensive OpenAI and Anthropic funding history article
detail: Pinggy Blog released a detailed timeline covering every financing round for OpenAI and Anthropic, from OpenAI's 2019 Microsoft partnership to Anthropic's $65 billion Series H in 2026. The article enumerates round sizes, valuations, lead investors, and notes how the capital is being allocated across product development and research. By aggregating public filings and press releases, the piece offers a single reference for the latest funding landscape of the two leading AI firms.
developments.why_it_matters: The consolidated funding overview lets investors, developers, and policymakers quickly assess the scale and direction of capital flowing into leading AI companies, informing strategic decisions and market analysis.

external_links.title: Racing to a Trillion: OpenAI and Anthropic's Funding History | Pinggy Blog

developments.title: Grok Bot gains Outlook, Calendar, and OneDrive plugins
detail: Grok Bot now includes three new plugins that let the AI read, write, and act across Microsoft accounts. The Outlook plugin enables searching, reading, and sending email as well as contact lookup; the Calendar plugin supports listing, creating, updating, and canceling events; the OneDrive plugin allows browsing, searching, and reading files.
These plugins are publicly listed on x.ai’s bot plugin directory, confirming they are shipped and usable today.
developments.why_it_matters: Bots can now automate email handling, schedule management, and file access directly within Microsoft services, expanding practical AI‑driven workflow capabilities.

developments.title: CallScript Enables Deterministic Code Mode via JSON Plans
detail: CallScript is a new tool that lets a language model write a restricted subset of JavaScript, which is then parsed into a JSON execution plan instead of being run directly. The JSON plan can be deterministically approved, stored, and resumed later, allowing consecutive calls to reference intermediate values without round‑tripping through the model’s context.
developments.why_it_matters: By converting generated code into auditable JSON plans, CallScript provides a way to enforce permission handling and security checks before execution, reducing the risk of unsafe code execution.

developments.title: CivilizationBench benchmark released
detail: CivilizationBench is introduced as a new benchmark designed to evaluate frontier AI technology. The creator positions it as a litmus test for measuring AI labs.
developments.why_it_matters: It provides a standardized way to compare AI labs' capabilities today.

developments.title: Muse Code exits beta, supports larger engineering tasks
detail: Muse Code has left its beta phase and is now engineered to handle bigger, more complex software development tasks. The tool can be installed with a single command line invocation, allowing developers to start using it immediately.
The announcement highlights that Muse Code is ready for production workloads, expanding its applicability beyond early testing scenarios.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers can now rely on Muse Code for substantial engineering projects, gaining immediate access via a one‑command install, which accelerates adoption and real‑world usage.

developments.title: Abliteration.ai releases abliterated-model-large-v2
detail: Abliteration.ai announced the release of abliterated-model-large-v2, a new large language model built on GLM‑5.3. The model is US‑hosted, runs in FP8 precision, and offers a 1 million token context window with zero input/output prompt retention.

According to the announcement, the model is designed for offensive cyber, red‑team, and agent‑testing tasks that other models avoid, providing capabilities for cyber exploitation and security research.
developments.why_it_matters: The model gives security researchers immediate access to a high‑capacity, US‑hosted LLM for red‑team operations and agent testing, expanding the toolset for offensive cyber work today.
